blocks.prompt: 1. Consider a data set at monthly sales figures. A polynomial regression model \(P(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 + x - 3\) is fitted to this data. If the observed sales in the \(5^{\text{th}}\) month are 240 units, find the percentage error.
blocks.explanation:
A regression model predicts a value; we compare the prediction with what really happened.
We must find the percentage error of the model in month 5.
Plan: predicted value \(= P(5)\) (the remainder on dividing by \(x - 5\)), then error \(=\) observed \(-\) predicted, then divide by the observed value and multiply by 100.
steps:
Given: \(P(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 + x - 3\); month \(x = 5\); observed sales \(= 240\) units.
To find: the percentage error.
Method: As in Example 8, Error \(=\) Observed \(-\) Predicted, and
\[\text{\% error} = \left|\dfrac{\text{Error}}{\text{Observed}}\right| \times 100\]
The predicted value is \(P(5)\), which by the Remainder Theorem is also the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - 5\).

Turn the words into numbers
\[x = 5\]
\[\text{Observed} = 240\]
\[\text{Predicted} = P(5)\]
Why: "5th month" is the input of the model, so \(x = 5\). The 240 units actually sold are the observed value.

Find the predicted value \(P(5)\)
\[P(5) = 5^3 + 2(5)^2 + 5 - 3\]
\[= 125 + 2(25) + 5 - 3\]
\[= 125 + 50 + 5 - 3\]
\[= 177\]
Why: The model's prediction for month 5 is its value at \(x = 5\). Powers first (\(5^3 = 125\), \(5^2 = 25\)), then multiply, then add and subtract.

Find the error
\[\text{Error} = 240 - 177\]
\[= 63\]
Why: Error is how far the real value is from the prediction: observed minus predicted. It is positive here, so the model predicted too few units.

Find the percentage error
\[\text{\% error} = \dfrac{|63|}{240} \times 100\]
\[= \dfrac{6300}{240}\]
\[= 26.25\]
Why: We compare the error with the observed (actual) value, exactly as Example 8 divides by the observed 40. The modulus keeps the percentage positive.

Check
\[26.25\% \text{ of } 240 = 0.2625 \times 240\]
\[= 63 \;\checkmark\]
\[177 + 63 = 240 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Taking the percentage of 240 gives back the error, and prediction plus error gives back the observed sales.
blocks.final_answer: Percentage error \(= 26.25\%\) (the model predicts \(P(5) = 177\) units, 63 below the observed 240).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key for Exercise 9.2 (book page 302, PDF 307) has 10 entries, but only 7 questions are printed (1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8), so its numbers do not line up with the questions. Key entry 1, \(26.25\%\), is this question's answer and agrees with our working. Key entries 2 ("\(x = -1\) is a valid point"), 5 ("CRC = 20") and 10 ("Code word is not valid, because \(x - 1\) is not a factor of \(C(x)\)") answer no printed question.
